sentences.text: th Order No. 05 /Dated: 8 May 2024 This interlocutory application has been filed for condoning the delay of 91 days in preferring L.P.A No. 60 of 2024.

2. Considering the facts and circumstances of this case and also after going through the cause shown in this interlocutory application seeking condonation of delay, we find sufficient grounds to condone the delay of 91 days and, accordingly, the present Interlocutory Application is allowed.

3. The appellant, namely, Sarju Kachhap is aggrieved by the order dated 4th October 2023 passed in W.P.(C) No. 3477 of 2022 by which the writ Court declined to issue a direction to the revenue authority to demarcate the land in Demarcation Case No. 37/2020-21.

4. Demarcation Case No. 37/2020-21 was instituted on an application submitted by the appellant on the ground that about 64 decimals land in Plot No. 485, 95 decimals in Plot No. 488, 58 decimals in Plot No. 850 and 10 decimals in Plot No. 858 within Khata No. 7 at Mouza Harmu within Circle Hehal belong to him and he was paying rent regularly to the State Government.
He filed the aforesaid application on 28th January 2020 and it was rejected by the Circle Officer, Hehal on 1st December 2020.
The appellant further pleaded that the aforementioned lands belonging to him were shown to have been acquired vide Gazette Notification No. 25 dated 17th June 1964 for Jharkhand State Housing Board.
He further pleaded that the compensation in lieu of the lands belonging to him was paid to Mangra Oraon, son of Late Sundra Oraon who was in no way related to him.
The appellant in support of his claim that the subject lands were recorded in his name produced Vanshawali certificate issued by the Circle Officer, Hehal.

However, the writ Court declined to interfere in the matter on the ground that in L.A. Case No.
19/1964-65 and L.A. Reference Case No. 700/1974 large chunk of lands were acquired for the Jharkhand State Housing Board and compensation was paid to the land owners/occupiers.
5.
Quite apparently, the writ petition involves serious disputed questions of fact which could not have been adjudicated in a proceeding under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.

Having regard to the fact that the writ petition itself was not maintainable, we are not inclined to defer hearing of this Letters Patent Appeal awaiting appearance of the learned counsel for the appellant.
6. L.P.A No. 60 of 2024 is dismissed.

However, the appellant is at liberty to work out his remedy as provided under the Land Acquisition Act by filing an application/petition/appeal for apportionment of compensation, challenging quantum of compensation or challenging the Award etc.
